questions.q: What did Balaam the prophet not do when he saw that it was good in the eyes of Yahweh to bless Israel?
questions.a: Balaam did not go somewhere else to find out what God wished, as he had previously.

questions.q: What happened when Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel camped, each in their own tribe?
questions.a: When Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel camped, the Spirit of God came on Balaam and he received a prophecy.

questions.q: What did Balaam do when he saw a vision from the Almighty?
questions.a: Balaam bowed down with his eyes open.

questions.q: What did Balaam say about the Israelites’ tents?
questions.a: Balaam said that the tents of the Israelites were very beautiful.

questions.q: What did Balaam say that the tents and dwellings of Israel were like?
questions.a: Balaam said that they were stretched out like wadis, like gardens upon a river, like aloes that Yahweh had planted, and like cedars upon water.

questions.q: What did Balaam say would happen for Israel?
questions.a: Balaam said that water would flow from his buckets, that his seed would be in many waters.

questions.q: Q: What did Balaam say about Israel’s king?
questions.a: Balaam said that Israel’s king would be higher than Agag and that his kingdom would be lifted up.

questions.q: What did Balaam say God was doing for Israel?
questions.a: Balaam said that God was bringing him out from Egypt, as the horns of a wild ox for him.

questions.q: What did Balaam say Israel would do to the nations who were his adversaries?
questions.a: Balaam said that he would devour the nations, crush their bones, and shatter them with his arrows.

questions.q: What did Balaam prophesy would happen to those who blessed or cursed Israel?
questions.a: Those who blessed Israel would be blessed and those who cursed Israel would be cursed.

questions.q: How did Balak show his anger against Balaam?
questions.a: Balak clapped his palms together.

questions.q: Who did Balak say kept Balaam from getting the promised reward?
questions.a: Balak said that Yahweh kept Balaam from getting his reward.

questions.q: What did Balaam say he had told the messengers whom Balak sent to him?
questions.a: Balaam said that even if Balak gave him the fullness of his house, silver and gold, he would not be able to pass over the mouth of Yahweh to do good or evil from his own heart, and that what Yahweh spoke, that he would speak.

questions.q: About what did Balaam counsel Balak before he returned to his own people?
questions.a: Balaam counseled Balak what Israel was going to do to Balak’s people in the end of the days.

questions.q: What did Balaam say that he heard, knew, and saw?
questions.a: Balaam said that he heard the words of God, knew the knowledge of the Most High, and saw the vision of the Almighty.

questions.q: What did Balaam see in his vision about Jacob and Israel?
questions.a: Balaam saw that a star has trodden from Jacob and a scepter has risen from Israel.

questions.q: What did Balaam say the star and scepter would do?
questions.a: Balaam said that it has shattered the edges of Moab and destroyed all the sons of Seth.

questions.q: What did Balaam say would happen to Edom and Seir?
questions.a: Balaam said that Edom would be a possession, and Seir, his enemies, would also be a possession.

questions.q: What did Balaam say that this person would do?
questions.a: Balaam said that that person would rule from Jacob and destroy a survivor from a city.

questions.q: What did Balaam say about Amalek, the first of nations?
questions.a: Balaam said that Amalek’s end would be unto destruction.

questions.q: What did Balaam say would happen to Kain?
questions.a: Balaam said that Kain would burn until Asshur took him captive.

questions.q: What did Balaam say about the dwelling of the Kenite?
questions.a: Balaam said that the Kenite’s dwelling was permanent and that his nest was set in the rock.

questions.q: What did Balaam say would come from the hand of Kittim, and what would they do?
questions.a: Balaam said that ships would come from the hand of Kittim and that they would afflict Asshur and afflict Eber.

questions.q: When Balaam ended his final prophecy, what did he do and what did Balak do?
questions.a: Balaam rose and went and returned to his place. Balak also went his way.

commentary.text: Balaam, leaving divinations, prophesies the happiness of Israel.

Verses 1–9 Now Balaam spake not his own sense, but the language of the Spirit that came upon him. Many have their eyes open who have not their hearts open; are enlightened, but not sanctified. That knowledge which puffs men up with pride, will but serve to light them to hell, whither many go with their eyes open. The blessing is nearly the same as those given before. He admires in Israel, their beauty. The righteous, doubtless, is more excellent than his neighbour. Their fruitfulness and increase. Their honour and advancement. Their power and victory. He looks back upon what had been done for them. Their power and victory. He looks back upon what had been done for them. Their courage and security. The righteous are bold as a lion, not when assaulting others, but when at rest, because God maketh them to dwell in safety. Their influence upon their neighbours. God takes what is done to them, whether good or evil, as done to himself. (Nu 24:10-14)

This vain attempt to curse Israel is ended. Balak broke out into a rage against Balaam, and expressed great vexation. Balaam has a very full excuse; God restrained him from saying what he would have said, and constrained him to say what he would not have uttered.

Under the powerful influence of the Spirit of prophecy, Balaam foretold the future prosperity and extensive dominion of Israel. Balaam boasts that his eyes are open. The prophets were in old times called seers. He had heard the words of God, which many do who neither heed them, nor hear God in them. He knew the knowledge of the Most High. A man may be full of the knowledge of God, yet utterly destitute of the grace of God. He calls God the Most High and the Almighty. No man could seem to express a greater respect to God; yet he had no true fear of him, love to him, nor faith in him; so far a man may go toward heaven, and yet come short of it at last. Here is Balaam's prophecy concerning Him who should be the crown and glory of his people Israel; who is David in the type; but our Lord Jesus, the promised Messiah, is chiefly pointed at, and of him it is an illustrious prophecy. Balaam, a wicked man, shall see Christ, but shall not see him nigh; not see him as Job, who saw him as his Redeemer, and saw him for himself. When he comes in the clouds, every eye shall see him; but many will see him, as the rich man in hell saw Abraham, afar off. He shall come out of Jacob, and Israel, as a Star and a Sceptre; the former denoting his glory and lustre; the latter his power and authority. Christ shall be King, not only of Jacob and Israel, but of all the world; so that all shall be either governed by his golden sceptre, or dashed in pieces by his iron rod. Balaam prophesied concerning the Amalekites and Kenites, part of whose country he had now in view. Even a nest in a rock will not be a lasting security. Here is a prophecy that looks as far forward as to the Greeks and Romans. He acknowledges all the revolutions of states and kingdoms to be the Lord's doing. These events will make such desolations, that scarcely any will escape. They that live then, will be as brands plucked out of the fire. May God fit us for the worst of times! Thus Balaam, instead of cursing the church, curses Amalek the first, and Rome the last enemy of the church. Not Rome pagan only, but Rome papal also; antichrist and all the antichristian powers. Let us ask ourselves, Do we in knowledge, experience, or profession, excel Balaam? No readiness of speech, even in preaching or prayer, no gifts of knowledge or prophecy, are in themselves different from, or superior to the boasted gifts of him who loved the wages of unrighteousness, and died the enemy of God. Simple dependence on the Redeemer's atoning blood and sanctifying grace, cheerful submission to the Divine will, constant endeavours to glorify God and benefit his people, these are less splendid, but far more excellent gifts, and always accompany salvation. No boasting hypocrite ever possessed these; yet the feeblest believer has something of them, and is daily praying for more of them.
